part.text:
The first thing you asked me to build was a function that adds a todo item to a list, in `todo.py`.

At the time, `add_todo(todos, item)` did exactly one thing: appended `item` (a plain string) to the `todos` list and returned the list. It raised `ValueError` if `item` was empty/falsy.

That's changed since then, when you asked for `complete_todo`, storing plain strings didn't leave anywhere to record a "done" flag, so I changed `add_todo` to store dicts instead: `{"text": item, "done": False}`. Later, when you asked for persistence, I added an optional `path` parameter so it can save to disk via `storage.py` after appending.

So the original, first version was narrower than what's in `todo.py` now: no `done` tracking, no persistence, just a bare append to a list of strings.
